sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r7/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 7 / check 6; Internal Quality Checks row 7, which says 'no network' but the delivery profile in SKILL.md says public network, which this task uses)
evidence: I checked each requirement in instruction.md and the three notes against the seed, the runtime and the graded criteria. Reachability: environment/Dockerfile installs express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 globally with NODE_PATH, as integration.md:3 says. test.sh:98-111 starts node /app/server.js as uid 65534 under env -i, with only PATH, NODE_PATH, HOME=$APP_COPY, PORT=3000 and DB_PATH. That matches integration.md:3. The seed has all 5 accounts, the timer options [null,1,7,30], 3 matters, the walled list for Dev on M-12, versions, holds, parents and read_up_to. Every seeded fact the criteria use can be derived from the seed plus the fixed clock in integration.md:7. Examples: K-10 (2026-05-05T11:00:00Z) is exactly seven days old on the 7-day M-11, so it is gone, while K-11 (+1 s) stays. K-1 is gone and leaves a placeholder over K-14/K-15. K-17 is held, sent 3 May, and is overdue once released. K-13 and K-18 are 8 and 9 days old when M-13 is cut to 7 days. K-7 is held. No browser in the agent image is needed to build the app. Network is public, so the brief's request to try it in a browser can be met by installing Playwright. The workbook counts the public internet as reachable. Single reading: the brief settles every graded behaviour in words. Examples: the exact-timer boundary (walls-and-retention.md 'a message sent exactly seven days ago ... is already gone'), editing does not make a message younger, a hold covers exactly one message, literal search for %, _ and *, substring search, the transcript heading, the time the transcript was generated, versions shown for a held edited message, a plain 'not available' for walled routes and other clients' matters, Enter/Shift+Enter/Escape, the confirm on delete, a highlight that lasts until something else is opened, and a refusal reason that stays in place. Where the brief really allows more than one design, the criteria accept them all. Examples: the JUDGE-W3 cross-matter reply is accepted whether it is refused or filed under its own parent's matter. The versions viewer in timer_changes is conditional ('If the app lets Harriet open earlier versions'). A delete confirm may be in the page or a browser dialog. Any clear time format is accepted. Clipboard and copy-box links are both handled in app_context. I tried a plausible broken app: one that shows earlier versions to clients, or that dedupes nothing on replay. The brief rules it out explicitly. I tried a conforming alternative that could fail: one where mark-unread puts the line below the message. The brief's 'moves the line there' and 'where I stopped reading' fix the line above that message, so it fails under the brief's own text. Residual readings, Note-level and not defects: (a) Sign-out is never named in the brief, but signin_and_client_scope and refusal_in_place sign out. 'Sign in as different people' implies it, and SKILL.md lists identity surfaces as a known false positive. (b) The link format is not specified. A link URL that contains the matter number (e.g. /matters/M-12#K-6), linkified in M-11, would show 'M-12' to walled Dev. walls-and-retention.md already forbids leaking by 'a link to one of its messages pasted somewhere they can see', and the golden uses an opaque /messages/K-6 (public/app.js:525-527), so the brief does tell a careful builder to avoid it. (c) For the JUDGE-W2 cross-matter reply, a builder could check 'same matter' before the wall and return a different refusal. The wall text ('asking the server for it ... nothing back but a plain "not available"') and 'Two things matter more than anything else' make the wall answer the governing reading. (d) test.sh tolerates symlinks inside /app/node_modules, which the brief forbids. This is lenient and never fails a conforming app. This is a source review only. No Docker or judge run was needed or performed for this row, and it does not attest any Oracle, model or portal score.
